id_and_class.summary: Raman argues that the arrival of consciousness, which he calls the ‘Third Big Bang’ after the origin of the universe and the origin of life, was a turning point in cosmic history. Humans are physically tiny and short-lived, but awareness is the screen on which colour, beauty, law, and meaning first appear, so consciousness makes us cosmically significant.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Universe's Third Big Bang

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a screen on which the attributes of the physical universe are projected and made known. Without it the cosmos would be mute matter with no colour, music, mathematics, or meaning.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Experience such as the golden sunset or the taste of honey depends on neurons firing in brains. Raman leaves open whether consciousness is a passing flicker or a small replica of the cosmic totality that Indic thinkers called Brahman.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Emergence as a major cosmic event, following the Big Bang and the origin of self-replicating life; Raman does not specify its metaphysical type
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Colours, scents, and tastes are not features of the world until sensing organisms respond to it. Before rods evolved in the retina, Raman says, there was no green grass or red rose.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A physical universe, life, brains, and conscious observers; possibly a cosmic totality of which human consciousness is a miniature.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Three cosmic ‘Big Bangs’: the physical origin of the universe, the emergence of self-replicating molecules, and the emergence of awareness. The second and third have probably happened elsewhere too.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness arrived late, after billions of years of an inert, insipid universe, and may either be extinguished in time or prove continuous with the whole cosmos.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In human brains and in other creatures' equivalent organs on Earth, and probably on other planets that host life.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness discovers and represents the universe in words and equations, and it also acts on the world, as when humans achieved nuclear fusion on Earth or photographed the planets.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Human minds turn the physical world into formulas, measurements, and stories, such as elliptical orbits, the inverse square law, and the indeterminacy principle, that did not exist before.
core_claims_and_evidence: Measured by size, strength, or longevity, humans count for almost nothing in a universe about fourteen billion years old.
Without conscious beings, none of the universe's light, beauty, or lawfulness would ever appear.
Consciousness injects or discerns meaning in an otherwise mindless, mechanical cosmos, which gives humans significance despite physical insignificance.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical reflection informed by physics and cosmology

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Raman's account addresses why consciousness matters, not what it is or how it arises. His phrase ‘injects or discerns meaning’ leaves open whether meaning is created by minds or found by them.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Raman does not decide whether consciousness is a passing flicker or a replica of a cosmic totality such as Brahman.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Compatible with naturalistic emergence and with Vedantic idealism alike, since Raman deliberately leaves the metaphysics open.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Raman leaves open whether consciousness is a passing flicker or part of a larger cosmic consciousness.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Raman holds that consciousness lights up the cosmos and gives meaning to a universe that would otherwise be silent and dark.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Raman’s Cosmic Significance, V. V. Raman (Landscape of Consciousness entry)
